data.one_liner: Pre‑built Flutter widgets for displaying Firebase Realtime Database data.
data.what_it_does: The package offers ready‑made UI components that connect to Firebase Realtime Database and automatically update when the data changes. It includes helpers for queries, pagination and common list/detail patterns, reducing boilerplate code.
use_when: You need a quick UI to show realtime data from Firebase without writing low‑level stream handling.
You are building admin panels, dashboards or simple list/detail screens that map directly to database nodes.
avoid_when: You require highly custom UI or complex interactions that the provided widgets cannot express.
Your app does not use Firebase or you prefer a different backend.
strengths: Speeds up development by providing ready‑made widgets.
Seamlessly integrates with FlutterFire and works on all major platforms.
Handles realtime streams and pagination out of the box.
weaknesses: Limited customization compared to building widgets manually.
Adds an extra dependency layer; breaking changes may require migration.
Only works with Firebase Realtime Database, not other backends.
data.setup_notes: Add firebase_core, firebase_database and firebase_ui_database to pubspec, initialize Firebase in main(), configure iOS/Android native Firebase files (Google‑Service‑Info.plist, google-services.json). No CocoaPods required after v3.0.0.

alternatives.name: firebase_database
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides low‑level access to Realtime Database without UI abstractions, giving full control.

alternatives.name: cloud_firestore
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer Firestore over Realtime Database, this package offers similar UI helpers for Firestore data.
